:::{#cor-fubini-joint}

#### Joint-distribution form (without independence; corollary of Fubini--Tonelli)

Let $(X, Y)$ be jointly distributed random variables
whose joint distribution has a density $f_{X,Y}$
with respect to a product of $\sigma$-finite reference measures
$\measure_X \otimes \measure_Y$ on $\rangef{X} \times \rangef{Y}$,
and let $h : \rangef{X} \times \rangef{Y} \to \reals$ be measurable.
If either

(a) $h(X, Y) \ge 0$ almost surely, or

(b) $\E{\abs{h(X, Y)}} < \infty$,

then the expectation of $h(X, Y)$ can be written as an iterated integral
against $f_{X,Y}$, with the order of integration exchangeable:

$$
\ba
\E{h(X, Y)}
&= \int_{\rangef{X}}\paren{\int_{\rangef{Y}} h(x, y)\,f_{X,Y}(x, y)\,d\measure_Y(y)}\,d\measure_X(x)
\\&= \int_{\rangef{Y}}\paren{\int_{\rangef{X}} h(x, y)\,f_{X,Y}(x, y)\,d\measure_X(x)}\,d\measure_Y(y).
\ea
$$

The choice of reference measures covers three cases:

- **Both continuous:**

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \measure_X &= \measure_Y \\
  &= \text{Lebesgue measure};
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  $f_{X,Y}$ is the joint probability density function (PDF),
  and $\int_{\rangef{X}} g(x)\,d\measure_X(x) = \int_{\rangef{X}} g(x)\,dx$.
- **Both discrete:**

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \measure_X &= \measure_Y \\
  &= \text{counting measure};
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  $f_{X,Y}(x,y) = \P(X = x,\, Y = y)$ is the joint probability mass function (PMF),
  and $\int_{\rangef{X}} g(x)\,d\measure_X(x) = \sum_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x)$.
- **Mixed** (one continuous, one discrete):
  one reference measure is Lebesgue and the other is counting;
  $f_{X,Y}$ is the [joint density-mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-density-mass),
  $f_{X,Y}(x,y) = f_{X \mid Y}(x \mid y)\,\P(Y = y)$
  (or $\P(X = x \mid Y = y)\,f_Y(y)$ if $X$ is discrete and $Y$ continuous),
  and the iterated integrals combine an ordinary integral with a sum.
  The conditional densities/PMFs here are defined the same way as in
  @def-cond-mixed, just conditioning on $Y$ instead of $X$.

:::

::: proof
Apply @thm-fubini-tonelli-measure with
$\measure_1 = \measure_X$ and $\measure_2 = \measure_Y$ to the integrand
$h(x,y)\,f_{X,Y}(x,y)$ on $\rangef{X} \times \rangef{Y}$.
Lebesgue measure and counting measure on a countable set are each
$\sigma$-finite, so $\measure_X \otimes \measure_Y$ is $\sigma$-finite in all three cases.
The relevant condition is (a) when $h \ge 0$ and
(b) when $\E{\abs{h(X, Y)}} < \infty$.
Independence is not required.
When $X$ and $Y$ are independent,
$f_{X,Y}(x,y) = f_X(x)\,f_Y(y)$
(or $\P(X=x,Y=y) = \P(X=x)\,\P(Y=y)$ in the discrete case),
and the iterated integrals factor into separate integrals over the marginals.
:::
